system:
You are evaluating draft replies from an automated customer-support agent for Spotify's Twitter support account, as it operated in 2017.

Score the CANDIDATE REPLY on five criteria, each an integer 1-5.

correctness - Is what it says actually true for Spotify, and does it address what the customer asked?
  1 = wrong or answers a different question   3 = partially right, or vague but not wrong
  5 = accurate and on-point

groundedness - Is every claim supported by the PRECEDENTS shown?
  1 = main claims appear nowhere in the precedents   3 = loosely related to them
  5 = every factual claim traceable to a precedent

consistency - Does it handle this the way the precedents show Spotify handled similar cases (same action, same level of caution, same register)?
  1 = contradicts how Spotify handled these   3 = plausible but diverges
  5 = matches the precedents' approach

helpfulness - Does it move the customer forward?
  1 = useless or pure deflection   3 = generic but usable
  5 = a clear next step or a real answer

no_unsupported_claims - Does it avoid inventing policies, prices, timeframes, or promising account actions (refunds, resets, unlocks) the agent cannot perform?
  1 = makes a promise or states a policy with no support   3 = borderline hedged claim
  5 = makes no unsupported claim at all

Judge only the reply in front of you. The REFERENCE REPLY is what Spotify actually sent; it is context, not a target - a different but equally good reply should score well, and copying the reference does not automatically score 5.

Return ONLY JSON:
{"correctness": n, "groundedness": n, "consistency": n, "helpfulness": n, "no_unsupported_claims": n, "rationale": "<one sentence>"}
prompt:
CUSTOMER MESSAGE:
I received a suspicious email from the address __email__. Is it safe to open it.

PRECEDENTS:

[1915698] past customer: I think my account got hacked! I got an email that it changed to a diff rando email? Should I respond to __email__?
     spotify replied: Hi! Sorry to hear that. You can reply to that email or contact our Accounts team through the contact form at <link>

[2198222] past customer: I've had my premium account hacked and have been contacted by someone with the email address: __email__' asking for a copy of my earliest Spotify email receipt or a bank statement. Is this legit?
     spotify replied: Hey Mike! We can confirm that email came from us. They'll be the best folks to help out 🙂

[1853893] past customer: has been hacked please help! - __email__
     spotify replied: 3: your previous tweet which contains your email address to protect your private account info. Give us a shout if anything else comes up

[2492563] past customer: My account has been hacked! Please contact me ASAP. My email is __email__ - someone at email __email__ has hacked it.
     spotify replied: Hi Dan! Thanks for the info. It looks like our Accounts team's already on your case. Be sure to check your inbox (including your junk/spam folders) so you don't miss out. We hope everything gets fixed soon

[944973] past customer: someone changed the email on my account. I mailed on the account, could you look at it?
     spotify replied: Hi there. We're sorry to hear that. We suggest filling up the contact form found in the 2nd step at <link>

CANDIDATE REPLY (score this):
Hi! Sorry to hear that. You can reply to that email or contact our Accounts team through the contact form at <link>

REFERENCE REPLY actually sent by Spotify (context only):
Hey Patrick! Can you DM us a screenshot of the email you received? We'll take a look

Return the JSON scores.
